title: Understanding the Loss Function
text: The loss function shown is a variation of the cross-entropy loss. Notice how the term for false negatives is modified by raising $$(1-p)$$ to the power of $$3$$. This modification affects the penalty for certain types of errors.

title: Comparing with Cross-Entropy Loss
text: In standard cross-entropy loss, the term $$\left(1-y\right) \ln\left(1-p\right)$$ is not raised to any power. Consider how raising $$(1-p)$$ to the power of $$3$$ might change the impact of false positive predictions.

hintAnswer: It increases the penalty for false positives.
title: Impact of the Power on $$(1-p)$$
text: What effect does raising $$(1-p)$$ to the power of $$3$$ have on the loss function?
choices: It increases the penalty for false positives.
It decreases the penalty for false positives.
It has no effect on the penalty for false positives.
